comments.content:
Any candidates of interest this week? I just realized that the recommended duration is until 1 February so I think we will need to settle up with the current top candidates (they seem solid!) 
Perhaps its worth focusing on the business development / investor relations talent? 
rfc (request for comment) @diamondnegroni

I made a custom label for 1 Month. I'm not sure if that will work. I suppose it would have been optimal to break down the campaign into smaller (per week) tasks 
Examples: 
1. post on RocketTalent (or whatever its called.)
2. post on linkedin
3. interviews
This detailed approach has several benefits:
1. work audibility
2. higher compensation in rewards
Although I understand this may have had a lot of friction because the payouts are only starting to work just this week. I appreciate your patience and I hope that you continue to try and become familiar with the system in order to increase your rewards compensation (while allowing us more opportunities to improve the system for non code deliverables!)
---
Lastly it is important to regularly post updates on the issues that you are assigned to or the bot will unassign you. We used to have a follow up feature but that hasn't been migrated over yet.

lol it worked thats crazy. In the future, lets not use the 1 month label. We should break this down into smaller tasks [as I mentioned above](https://github.com/ubiquity/recruiting/issues/3#issuecomment-1946123760). 
You should create those proposals for your upcoming weeks of work, and I can set prices for them on whenever I get chances to review your proposals. This will allow us to 1. stay in sync 2. share information transparently with the organization (very useful when you have team members working directly with you) and 3. receive rewards.

They can certainly contribute in the public DevPool. If they prove themself then we can extend an offer. I'm skeptical because from the surface they seem a bit green.
Automation shows its power when you run massive numbers (think like 10'000+) but the response rate is lower than I expect. Perhaps you can share what you sent so I can help you out.
We can do English only if that helps!
We're just about out of time on the project. I presume that you were unable to find another viable TypeScript candidate in Seoul?

As mentioned in the performance review. I think that this was technically accomplished but I think that one of the candidates is better suited for research. As such, I'll still need to continue active recruiting efforts for more TypeScript developers.

- With the intent to transition them to in-office work.
- Recommended duration: 1 December to 1 February
For
- Bot maintenance
- Dollar UI maintenance.
- More are always welcomed, although we may have them contribute strictly via the DevPool (no/low base pay)
